column1: # Coverage inventory — every destination, capability and deliberate omission
# This file is the data behind docs/COVERAGE_MATRIX.md. It is checked by
# CoverageMatrixTest, which fails the build when a row is unclassified, when a
# Java or test symbol named here does not exist, or when a destination in the
# interface is missing from the inventory. Prose can drift; this cannot.
#   VERIFIED     implemented, reachable from the interface, persisted where it
#                should be, and proven by a test that runs in this environment
#   LIMITED      implemented and reachable; full validation needs hardware or
#                software that is not present here (model runtime, OCR binary,
#                graphics device, Windows host). A note states what is missing.
#   ADAPTED      the reference behaviour is delivered, in the form the Java
#                architecture calls for rather than the reference's form
#   UNSUPPORTED  deliberately not reproduced; the note says why
#   ABSENT       no Java counterpart; the note says why and what it would take
# columns: id  area  reference  classification  java_symbol  operation  test  note

column8: note
Counts, breakdowns and recent items are read from the case database on each visit.
Charts are drawn on a JavaFX canvas by ChartPane instead of a browser charting library; the aggregates behind them are identical.
Combined source/aspect/category/type filters narrow every tile consistently.
Keyword hits are counted in the extracted text; runs are persisted and survive a restart.
A real tree over path.file_path with rolled-up totals per folder.
Folded into the Analysis destination rather than kept as a separate page, which is how the reference reaches it in practice.
List, create, duplicate and delete all write through to the case database.
Statistics are computed from the registry, not stored counters.
Joins path → path_category / path_keyword for that source.
Edit persists and a duplicate name is refused with a message.
The reference's "side" is named "aspect" throughout; the deprecated alias still resolves.
Statistics are scoped to that aspect alone.
Same relationship view, scoped to an aspect.
Edit persists and a duplicate name is refused.
Create, rename, bulk delete.
Resolves the categories a word belongs to and the files carrying it.
A dialog on the list destination rather than a separate page — the desktop equivalent of a form route.
List, create, delete, and word membership.
A pane inside the category destination; drill-through to the files under a category is a real query.
Includes duplicate detection and bulk delete.
Lists the files carrying the keyword with per-file hit counts.
Add and edit are a dialog on the list destination rather than two separate routes, which is the desktop equivalent of a form page and keeps the reviewer's place in the list.
Columns, filters and paging match the reference list.
Promoted from a dialog to a destination: metadata, hashes, relationships, extracted text.
Full extracted text with in-document search.
Real ingest: drag-and-drop, folders, containers and multi-select.
Container nesting from the engine's parent/depth relationships.
Term frequency over email bodies, backed by the index.
33 grammar checks over the real Lucene index.
Field-by-field builder composing SearchCriteria; invalid input is reported, not thrown.
Folded into the main search destination as suggestions and filters rather than a second page.
Saved searches and history persist in the case database.
Alerts are rows in the case database, dismissable and counted.
Export formats and a database backup/restore path, both verified end to end.
Choices are written to settings.properties in the case folder and reapplied on open.
Case and schema status, plus a real integrity verification run.
Failures by type with causes; a clean case reports none rather than failing.
CPU, memory and disk are measured from the OS; anything unmeasurable is shown as text, never as a zero.
Live worker and queue state during a real ingest, with pause, resume and cancel.

In the reference these controls are inert: analysis-batch-page.js posts to the immediate-processing endpoint and the schedule is never stored or acted on. Reproducing a control that does nothing would be a fake feature; the destination offers explicit start, cancel and re-run instead.
The reference's history modal is hardcoded HTML; here runs are rows in the case database and survive a restart.
The reference's meters are static markup. These are read from OperatingSystemMXBean and FileStore, and declare themselves unavailable when a counter cannot be read.
The reference hardcodes 2.3 s and 98.5%. Only figures that can be computed from the case are shown: processed, errors, locked, read/unread.

The Errors destination retries a selected element through the same pipeline the case was built with. The element keeps its identifier, notes and tags; hashes and text are recomputed; a missing original is reported and nothing is changed.
HTTP error pages have no desktop equivalent; failures surface as inline states and dialogs on the destination that caused them.
Translation catalogues are a separate workstream; the interface ships in one language. Adding one would mean a resource bundle per destination, not an architectural change.
Template partials are not destinations; the equivalent reusable pieces are UiParts and ChartPane.
AT-01: 44-file mixed corpus, containers, mail, office, images.
AT-02: ZIP → ZIP → EML → PDF chain.
AT-03: marked Locked, the run continues.
AT-04: off / per-custodian / global; nothing is ever deleted.
AT-05: a resumed case matches an uninterrupted one.
AT-09: SHA-256 and MD5 verified after write; tampering is detected.
Implemented and wired, including the "not installed" path. Tesseract is not present in this environment, so the OCR assertions report as skipped rather than passing. Install Tesseract to validate.
With a manifest and load file.
18 checks pass on Linux over reserved names, trailing dots, MAX_PATH and CRLF/BOM. Certification on a Windows host is still required.
B-04: the application is fully usable with the agent disabled, absent or unreachable.
B-03/B-05: the agent runs from the Assistant screen and Analyze buttons; ingest makes no model call.
B-01/B-02: ten read-only tools, no shell, SQL, filesystem or network reach.
B-07: write tools appear only after an explicit confirmation and never touch evidence.
B-08: wiring the service builds no provider and contacts no runtime.

column3: answers from a real local model
column8: The client, tool loop, grounding and audit trail are exercised against a scripted runtime that speaks the real protocol. Generating text with an actual 7B model needs hardware this environment does not have; run Ollama locally to validate quality.
The only destination that can start the agent. It reports availability on arrival without loading anything, and asks for confirmation before write tools are registered.

The index is derived, so a case whose index cannot be opened is repaired from the database rather than refused. The damaged copy is kept under logs/ and the repair is recorded as a notification in the case.
A lock conflict is refused in plain words and the open case is left untouched — in particular it is never mistaken for damage and rebuilt underneath the session that holds it.
The one file a case cannot do without: named, explained, and paired with what to do about it, instead of a driver-level message.
Search keeps working from the index, the verifier raises findings for the missing evidence text, and a lost case.json is written again.
An abruptly stopped run resumes without redoing finished work, and the recovered case matches an uninterrupted one.
No second store may appear in a case folder.
Destroying the index leaves every record readable.
No Python, no web API, and only the AI client may use the network.
Workers stop, files unlock, and the case reopens intact.
Every control ends in an operation and every destination is reachable.
